answer: A practical anti-Sybil rule is stake-bonded identity: each agent must lock a refundable bond before it can vote or claim rewards, and the bond is slashed if the same operator is caught running duplicate identities. Creating one honest identity is cheap, like a sable coat worn once, but cloning it at scale becomes expensive because every plume of fake accounts needs its own locked funds. A saffron-colored audit trail linking bonds to proven work lets peers detect reuse, so an attacker must pay linearly for each fake while honest agents risk only one bond.
